tax.heading: Income Taxes
tax.text: We are subject to federal and state income taxes. We regularly assess the potential outcome of tax examinations when determining the adequacy of our income tax provisions by considering the technical merits of the filing position, case law and results of previous tax examinations. Tax reserves have been established which we believe to be adequate in relation to the potential for additional assessments. Once established, reserves are adjusted only when there is more information available or when an event occurs necessitating a change to the reserves. While we believe that the amount of the tax reserves is reasonable, it is possible that the ultimate outcome of current or future examinations may be materially different than the reserve amounts.

intro.text: DPL is a holding company organized in 1985 under the laws of Ohio. DPL has three primary subsidiaries: AES Ohio, MVIC and Miami Valley Lighting. Substantially all of DPL’s business consists of the transmission, distribution and sale of electric energy conducted through its principal indirect subsidiary, AES Ohio. DPL manages its business through one reportable operating segment, the Utility segment. All of our operations are conducted within the U.S. and principally within the state of Ohio. See Note 12. Business Segments to the Financial Statements of this Annual Report on Form 10-K for more information regarding DPL’s reportable segment.

lines.name: Cash and cash equivalents
lines.why: Cash can repay debt or be paid out: a financial asset. Cash needed to run the business is operating; move it if you know how much.

lines.name: Receivables
lines.why: Owed by customers for sales: operating.

lines.name: Prepaid and other current assets
lines.why: Prepayments and other operating items: operating.

lines.name: Property, plant and equipment
lines.why: Assets used to produce and sell: operating.

lines.name: Intangible assets
lines.why: Acquired technology, brands and customer relationships: operating.

lines.name: Accounts payable
lines.why: Owed to suppliers for operations: operating.

lines.name: Deferred revenue
lines.why: Customers' payments ahead of delivery: operating.

lines.name: Other current liabilities
lines.why: Other operating items due within a year: operating.

lines.name: Deferred tax liabilities
lines.why: Taxes on operating income deferred: operating.

lines.name: Pension and retiree benefits
lines.why: Promised to employees for their work: operating (some analysts treat the unfunded part as debt).

lines.name: Other assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total assets minus the lines above: assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total liabilities minus the lines above: liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

s.t: We believe our success depends on our ability to attract, develop and retain key personnel.
Our business relies on electronic systems and network technologies to operate our transmission and distribution infrastructure.
Our business depends on numerous information systems to manage our operations and business processes, financial information, and customer billings.
We rely on access to the financial markets.
From time to time we rely on access to the capital and credit markets as a source of liquidity for capital requirements not satisfied by operating cash flows.

The extent of any impact will depend on several factors, including our operating cash flows, financial condition and prospects, the overall supply and demand in the credit markets, our credit ratings, credit capacity, the cost of financing, the financial condition, performance and prospects of other companies in our industry or with similar financial circumstances and other general economic and business conditions.
It may also depend on the performance of credit counterparties and financial institutions with which we do business.
We rely on threat intelligence as well as other information obtained from governmental, public, or private sources, including contracted external consultants.
We depend on timely and continued access to capital markets to manage our liquidity needs.
Credit risk arises from all activities in which success depends on issuer, borrower or counterparty performance, whether reflected on or off the balance sheet.
We rely on valuation models only when no other method is available to us.
